question: Transmission-based precautions are utilized as which tier of basic infection control?
explanation: Transmission-based precautions serve as the second tier of basic infection control, applied in addition to standard precautions for specific pathogens. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of implementing transmission-based precautions?

options.B: To interrupt the chain of infection for specific pathogens
options.C: To lower the cost of hospital-acquired medications
options.D: To eliminate the need for hand hygiene

explanation: These specific measures are critical to interrupt the chain of infection when pathogens are known or suspected to be epidemiologically important. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h1)

question: To which group of patients must standard precautions be applied?

options.A: Only patients with confirmed infectious diseases
options.B: Only patients admitted to surgical wards
options.C: All patients regardless of their diagnosis or infection status
options.D: Only patients showing symptoms of respiratory distress

explanation: Standard precautions form the foundational layer and must be applied to the care of all patients regardless of their diagnosed or presumed infection status. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h2)

question: Which of the following is considered a key element of standard precautions?

options.A: Wearing an N95 respirator for all routine bed baths
options.B: Rigorous hand hygiene before and after patient contact
options.C: Placing all patients in a negative pressure isolation room
options.D: Avoiding the use of gloves entirely to improve tactile sensation

explanation: Key elements of standard precautions include rigorous hand hygiene before and after patient contact, safe injection practices, and appropriate PPE use. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h2)

question: Which of the following conditions typically requires the implementation of contact precautions?
explanation: Contact precautions are used for multi-drug resistant organisms like MRSA, as well as C. difficile and scabies. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h3)

question: What personal protective equipment is specifically required when entering a contact precaution room?
explanation: Nurses must don a clean, non-sterile gown and gloves upon entering a contact precaution room and remove them before leaving. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h3)

question: What is the typical distance that infectious droplets travel before settling?

options.C: Fifty feet in a straight line
options.D: They remain suspended indefinitely like airborne particles

explanation: Droplets travel short distances, usually three feet or less, and do not remain suspended in the air for long periods. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h4)

question: Which barrier method is required when entering the room of a patient on droplet precautions?
explanation: Healthcare workers must wear a standard surgical mask upon entering the room of a patient on droplet precautions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h4)

question: Which of the following diseases requires the implementation of airborne precautions?
explanation: Pulmonary or laryngeal tuberculosis, measles, and varicella zoster are classic examples requiring airborne precautions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h5)

question: What type of room engineering control is specifically required for patients on airborne precautions?

options.B: Standard medical ward with open windows only
options.C: Airborne Infection Isolation Room (AIIR) with negative pressure
options.D: Reversed isolation room for immunocompromised care

explanation: Patients must be placed in an Airborne Infection Isolation Room (AIIR) featuring negative air pressure and proper air filtration. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h5)

question: What is the first step when donning personal protective equipment (PPE) before entering a patient's room?
explanation: Donning must begin with performing hand hygiene before putting on any barrier items. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which item of PPE is typically removed first when doffing after patient care?
explanation: The CDC-recommended doffing order for most scenarios begins with removing the gloves, as they are typically the most contaminated item. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h6)

question: What is the practice of housing patients infected with the same microorganism in the same room called?
explanation: Cohorting involves placing patients infected or colonized with the same micro-organism in the same room when single rooms are unavailable. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h7)

question: When a patient on droplet or airborne precautions must be transported outside their room, what must the nurse ensure?

options.A: The patient wears no mask to facilitate breathing
options.B: The patient wears an appropriate barrier, such as a surgical mask
options.C: The patient walks without assistance through the main lobby
options.D: The receiving department is kept uninformed to reduce panic

explanation: If transport is required, the patient must wear appropriate barriers like a surgical mask, and receiving departments must be notified in advance. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h7)

question: Which of the following is a practical adaptation for hand hygiene in resource-limited Nigerian community settings?

options.A: Closing all clinics until running indoor plumbing is installed
options.B: Using improvised handwashing stations such as Veronica buckets
options.C: Eliminating hand hygiene protocols due to lack of sinks
options.D: Using dry cloth towels exclusively without water or soap

explanation: Improvised handwashing stations like Veronica buckets are practical, life-saving adaptations for hand hygiene where running water is limited. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h8)

question: What is a key responsibility of community health nurses regarding infectious diseases in local settings?

options.A: Waiting for national directives before taking local action
options.B: Prioritizing syndromic surveillance to detect outbreaks early at the grassroots level
options.C: Discouraging community members from seeking traditional medical advice
options.D: Restricting all healthcare outreach programs permanently

explanation: Community health nurses must prioritize syndromic surveillance to detect infectious disease outbreaks early at the grassroots level. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h8)
